patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient experienced sudden loss of consciousness while pitching in a baseball game. No history of trauma associated with the event. The patient regained consciousness after receiving cardiopulmonary resuscitation.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Active, with regular participation in sports. No use of tobacco, alcohol, or recreational drugs reported.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Negative for headaches, seizures, chest pain, palpitations, shortness of breath, or dizziness prior to the event.

objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with sudden loss of consciousness and no prior history of neurological or cardiovascular problems.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I passed out suddenly while pitching during a baseball game and had to be revived with CPR. I didn’t have headaches, seizures, chest pain, palpitations, shortness of breath, or dizziness beforehand.

I’m sorry that happened. **One question at a time**:

**1) After you regained consciousness, did you have any confusion, weakness/numbness, or trouble speaking (even briefly)?**
Patient: I didn’t notice any confusion, weakness or numbness, or trouble speaking after I regained consciousness.
**2) Did anyone notice any abnormal movements during the episode** (e.g., shaking/jerking, tongue biting, or loss of bladder/bowel control)?

Doctor: Did anyone notice any abnormal movements during the episode—shaking/jerking, tongue biting, or loss of bladder/bowel control? Patient: No one reported any shaking or jerking, and there was no tongue biting or loss of bladder or bowel control that I’m aware of.
**3) Do you remember anything about the moment right before you passed out—any warning at all (e.g., nausea, sweating, visual changes, feeling hot, or a “wave” sensation)?**
Patient: I don’t recall any warning signs—no nausea, sweating, visual changes, feeling hot, or any “wave” sensation right before I passed out.
**4) Do you have any history of heart disease, fainting episodes before, or a family history of sudden cardiac death (especially at a young age)?**
Patient: I’ve never had fainting episodes before, and I don’t have any known heart disease. I’m not aware of any family history of sudden cardiac death at a young age.
**5) During the episode, did you have any chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath right before or after (even if you didn’t feel dizzy)?**
Patient: No—I didn’t have any chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath right before or after the episode.
**6) What was your age, and do you have any known medical conditions or take any medications/supplements (including stimulants like ADHD meds, pre-workout, or performance-enhancing substances)?**
Patient: I’m 23, and I don’t have any known medical conditions. I don’t take any medications or supplements, and I wasn’t using anything like stimulants or pre-workout.
**7) Were you dehydrated, overheated, or did you have any recent illness/fever, vomiting/diarrhea, or poor fluid intake?**
Patient: I wasn’t overheated, and I don’t recall being dehydrated. I didn’t have a recent illness or fever, and I didn’t have vomiting or diarrhea or poor fluid intake beforehand.
**8) Did the event occur during exertion/strenuous activity only (like pitching), and did you feel normal during the rest of the game before it happened?**
Patient: Yes, it happened while I was pitching—right during strenuous activity—and I felt normal and fine during the rest of the game right up until I suddenly passed out.
**9) After resuscitation, did you have any persistent symptoms** (e.g., ongoing shortness of breath, chest discomfort, severe headache, or weakness), or did you feel mostly back to baseline?

Patient: After I was revived, I didn’t have ongoing shortness of breath or chest discomfort, and I felt mostly back to my normal baseline afterward. I don’t recall any severe headache, weakness, or other lingering symptoms.
**10) Do you know what the CPR/“revived” rhythm was (e.g., shockable like VF/VT vs not shockable), or did they mention an AED shock?**
I don’t know what the CPR/“revived” rhythm was, and nobody mentioned whether an AED shock was delivered. They told me I was successfully revived with CPR, and I’ve mostly felt back to baseline since.
**11) Did you have any recent stimulant-like exposures besides meds—such as energy drinks, alcohol binge, recreational drugs (cocaine/amphetamines), or toxins?**
Patient: I didn’t have any energy drinks, alcohol binge, recreational drugs, or any other toxin exposure beforehand. I’ve been otherwise healthy and hadn’t taken anything unusual.
**12) Did you have any skin findings or recent infections (e.g., rash, fever, sores), or any known bleeding/bruising problems?**
Patient: I didn’t have any rash, fever, sores, or any recent infection, and I’m not aware of any unusual bruising or bleeding problems.
**13) Any history of asthma/COPD, wheezing, or chronic lung issues—or was this purely a sudden collapse without breathing symptoms?**
Patient: I don’t have asthma or any chronic lung issues, and I wasn’t wheezing or having breathing problems before or after the collapse.
**14) Did you have any head/neck trauma during the fall, and have you had any ongoing neurologic symptoms since?**
Patient: I didn’t have any known head or neck trauma during the fall, and I haven’t had any ongoing neurologic symptoms since I was revived.
